## Context / Problem

`tests/unit/test_changed_criteria.py` starts the CLI as the bare command `rebar` (lines 55, 248, 366). The child runs whichever `rebar` comes first on `PATH`, not the build under test. On a host where `~/.local/bin` (an older pipx install) precedes the worktree venv, 11 of the module's 18 tests fail with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'rebar.llm.evals'` raised from the pipx copy's `rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py`. With `.venv/bin` first on `PATH` all 18 pass. CI passes because its runner has no other `rebar` on `PATH`.

Reproduced 2026-11-03 (session a85e3cd3) at `0e7401446c5`: `.venv/bin/pytest -p no:xdist tests/unit/test_changed_criteria.py` with ambient `PATH` gave 11 failed, 7 passed; `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH"` gave 18 passed.

## Scope: the whole class, not one module

A syntax-tree scan of `tests/` found the same PATH dependence at 38 sites in 22 modules besides this one:

- 35 real child-process calls (`subprocess.run`/`Popen`/`check_output`/`check_call`/`call`) whose argv begins with the literal `"rebar"`, in 19 modules (the `test_identity_*` family, `test_verify_opcert*`, `test_guides.py`, `test_reclaim_collapse.py`, `test_opcert_rollback.py`, `test_mcp_opcert_signing_goose.py`, `reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_store.py`, and `interfaces/contracts/test_mcp_error_envelope*.py` / `test_workflow_error_codes_dbca.py`).
- 3 `shutil.which("rebar")` lookups: `tests/interfaces/store/sync_contention_harness.py:33` (prefers PATH's copy over the build), `tests/integration/test_store_concurrency.py:19`, and `tests/unit/test_llm_framework_docs.py:94` (runs documented `rebar ...` argv as-is).

The 22 files, under `tests/`: `integration/test_store_concurrency.py`, `interfaces/contracts/test_mcp_error_envelope.py`, `interfaces/contracts/test_mcp_error_envelope_happy.py`, `interfaces/contracts/test_workflow_error_codes_dbca.py`, `interfaces/store/sync_contention_harness.py` (helper; its consumers are `test_show_no_stall.py`, `test_reads_under_sync_contention.py`, `test_bridge_preview_under_sync_contention.py`), `unit/reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_store.py`, `unit/test_guides.py`, `unit/test_identity_3183.py`, `unit/test_identity_4e9d.py`, `unit/test_identity_ac7_bff8.py`, `unit/test_identity_ddbe.py`, `unit/test_identity_enforce_since_grandfather.py`, `unit/test_identity_gate_archived_and_unresolvable.py`, `unit/test_identity_gate_scope_and_ledger.py`, `unit/test_identity_ts3_117b.py`, `unit/test_identity_txn_signing.py`, `unit/test_llm_framework_docs.py`, `unit/test_mcp_opcert_signing_goose.py`, `unit/test_opcert_rollback.py`, `unit/test_reclaim_collapse.py`, `unit/test_verify_opcert.py`, `unit/test_verify_opcert_ac_coverage.py`.

All 189 tests in those 22 modules currently pass under the stale `PATH` only because the old global copy happens to support their commands; they break the same way once those commands change.

`sync_contention_harness.py`'s preference was introduced in `814d1a52143` and hoisted unchanged in `ecc5c8df623`; neither records a reason. The console script (`rebar.cli:main`) and `python -m rebar` (`src/rebar/__main__.py`) both call `rebar._cli.main(sys.argv[1:])`, so nothing there needs an installed console script.

## Plan

1. Convert every site to the established pattern `[sys.executable, "-m", "rebar", ...]` (already used at 14 sites, e.g. `tests/unit/test_cross_session_cli.py`, `tests/integration/test_init_fail_closed.py`). For `test_llm_framework_docs.py`, map a documented `rebar` argv[0] to `sys.executable -m rebar` and drop the `which` skip. For `test_store_concurrency.py`, replace the `_REBAR` path with a command prefix. No behaviour change in what each test asserts.
2. Add `tests/unit/test_no_bare_rebar_subprocess.py`, a `repo_policy` syntax-tree check over `tests/` (via `_tree_scan.parsed_python_files`) that fails, naming file:line, on (a) any call to a subprocess-launching function whose first argv element is the literal `"rebar"`, and (b) any `shutil.which("rebar")`. It ignores argv lists that are not passed to a subprocess launcher (fake runners and assertions such as `tests/scripts/test_canary_bridge.py`). It carries its own synthetic positive and negative samples so it cannot pass vacuously. No autouse fixtures, no new mechanism.
3. Evidence: run `test_changed_criteria.py` and all 22 converted modules with a fake `rebar` (a script that exits 99) first on `PATH`, before and after the change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/unit/test_changed_criteria.py` and the 22 other modules listed above start the CLI as `sys.executable -m rebar` (no bare `rebar`, no `shutil.which("rebar")`), and all of them (with the harness's 3 consumer modules standing in for the harness) pass with a fake `rebar` that exits 99 placed first on `PATH`.
- [ ] Before the change, the same fake-`rebar`-first run fails `test_changed_criteria.py` (recorded on this ticket with counts).
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_no_bare_rebar_subprocess.py` fails when a test subprocess starts the CLI by the bare name `rebar` or looks it up with `shutil.which("rebar")`, and passes on the converted tree; its synthetic samples prove both detections fire and that a non-subprocess `["rebar", ...]` list is not flagged.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass with the worktree `.venv/bin` first on `PATH`; the change lands through Gerrit with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`.
